S19 resolution step — confirm or consciously drop order_candidates_local_first's guarantees before sop_executor.rs is deleted. sop_executor.rs::order_candidates_local_first (with 5 passing unit tests) provides three specific guarantees over `.hex/project.json` -> inference.tier_models[t2/t2.5] read as an array: (1) locals (no vendor '/' in the name) always precede clouds regardless of configured order, (2) a known-good local coder (qwen2.5-coder:32b) is always appended as a terminal fallback if absent, (3) order-preserving dedup. Planner-time comparison against the three candidate surviving mechanisms found NONE to be a full equivalent: (a) hex-nexus/src/adapters/inference_router/tier_config.rs::TierModelConfig (ADR-2026-04-12-0202, the CLAUDE.md-documented tiered-inference system, tested in hex-nexus/tests/tier_routing.rs) maps each tier to a SINGLE scalar model string, not an ordered multi-candidate array — no local-first reordering, no fallback guarantee, no dedup; (b) hex-nexus/src/routes/inference.rs has two adjacent-but-different mechanisms: a provider-*type* priority chain (ollama/vllm/llama-cpp before openai-compat, ~line 126) and a narrower one-shot local-fallback-on-OpenRouter-exhaustion (lines ~816-838, reads the same tier_models.t2 key but only fires after ALL free-tier cloud attempts fail, and only picks ONE model, not a full reordered list); (c) hex-exec/src/direct_react.rs::candidate_models is precedence-based (explicit > configured-array-as-is > single > hardcoded default pair "devstral-small-2:24b"/"qwen2.5-coder:14b") with zero local-first reordering, zero terminal-fallback guarantee, and zero dedup. Confirm this comparison (re-verify by reading the three files) and write the one-line resolution note for the eventual excision commit message: state explicitly that the local-first-reordering + dedup + guaranteed-local-terminal-fallback behavior over a multi-candidate array is consciously dropped (no surviving path reproduces all three), OR port order_candidates_local_first (it is a pure fn, trivially portable) into hex-exec::candidate_models and/or routes/inference.rs before proceeding, if the operator wants to preserve it.

review_tiers.rationale: Non-destructive rewires (pool_autopause, supervisor_subscriber) plus the routes/sop.rs consumer removal — each drops a dependency on sop_executor/persona_prompt_seeds without deleting either file yet. Reviewed as one batch because they're mechanically similar (call-site + doc-comment removal) and independently revertible; closed by an interim cargo check --workspace so a bad rewire is caught before the irreversible deletions in tier 3.

The S19 model-fallback-equivalence resolution is a judgment call, not a mechanical edit — it decides whether a tested behavioral guarantee is silently lost. Reviewed alone so the operator can weigh in on 'drop and document' vs. 'port order_candidates_local_first forward' before the only implementation is deleted in tier 3.

The core irreversible deletion tier: sop_executor.rs (2059 lines) and persona_prompt_seeds.rs (464 lines) are deleted in dependency order, mod.rs's registry is edited to match, and the tier closes with the full cargo check --workspace + hex analyze hex-nexus gate (S10/S11). This is the highest-risk tier and should get the most careful review — it's where ~2500 LOC of the ~20-25k LOC ADR-2606071340 target actually leaves the tree.

Low-risk, mutually-independent cleanups with no compile dependency on each other: a doc-comment update (classifier_adapter.rs), three stale-comment rewrites in files outside the 6 named consumers, the HEX_SOP_* env-var write-site retirement (a scope addition discovered during planning-time grep, beyond the originally named 6 files), and the CLAUDE.md rule 11 rewrite. Reviewed together as a batch since none blocks the others; closed by the negative-spec grep sweep (S12/S13/S16).

Final sign-off: rebuild + restart the actual binary and probe runtime behavior (404s, hex do smoke test, functional-role preambles), then run the full hex dev validate suite and confirm the three explicitly-out-of-scope org-sim remnants (S18: adversarial_swarm.rs, twin_deterministic.rs, adapters/spacetime_persona.rs) were never touched.
